To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have extended SLURM to allow the use of remote GPU virtualization, and we have demonstrated that this new scheduling approach is beneficial for the users of the system.
SLURM support for remote GPU virtualizations can increase the flexibility of the job scheduler in a cluster.
We introduce a novel type of device in the job manager of a cluster, "rgpu" (remote GPU), to allow any application node to access to any GPU node using rCUDA as remote GPU virtualization technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel resource manager plugin for SLURM that allows the scheduling of GPU jobs in a cluster in a way that the GPUs can be accessed by the application running on any node in the cluster.
the development of a novel scheduling strategy for SLURM, which allows the use of GPUs in the cluster in a more efficient and transparent way.
the integration of a new type of GPU resource, rgpu, in the SLURM resource manager, and with the performance evaluation of the resulting system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SLURM is now ready to be used with remote GPU virtualization solutions, such as rCUDA, in order to provide users with a transparent and flexible access to the GPUs in a cluster.
our new rgpu device allows SLURM to schedule jobs in a more flexible manner, and that the new device does not introduce any overhead in the scheduling process.
our new SLURM implementation allows for a more efficient use of GPUs in the cluster, as the jobs can be scheduled in a more flexible way, taking into account all available GPUs in the cluster.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SLURM is now a complete solution for GPU virtualization.
SLURM is now a viable option for remote GPU virtualizations.
SLURM is now able to schedule tasks that can use GPUs from any node in the cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SLURM is an appropriate resource manager for GPU virtualization, and that it can be easily extended to support remote GPUs.
SLURM can be easily extended to manage heterogeneous resources such as GPUs and, with the right scheduling policy, the cluster performance can be greatly improved.
the new SLURM support for rgpu devices allows to achieve a better utilization of GPUs and, as a result, to reduce the execution time of the applications.
